# Project: Agentic HITL Medical Annotation

TU Delft Master's thesis research project by the user (Tijmen Meijer). A human-in-the-loop (HITL) system where LLM-based agents annotate medical text and iteratively improve via feedback from doctors (and auto-reviewers).

## Research questions

**Main:** How can a human-in-the-loop feedback mechanism improve the accuracy and reliability of medical text annotations generated by LLM-based agents?

**Sub-questions:**
1. What types of qualitative human feedback (error categorization, contextual explanations, domain-specific corrections) are most effective in improving prompt refinement? *(in progress)*
2. What prompt engineering techniques (few-shot, chain-of-thought, structured outputs) benefit most from human feedback integration? *(in progress)*
3. How does prompt complexity evolve across iterations, and what is the relationship between prompt length/structure and annotation accuracy? *(not yet)*
4. How many iteration cycles are required for convergence across different medical text types? *(not yet)*

Current focus: sub-questions 1 and 2.

## System layout

- [src/main.py](src/main.py) — entry point / iteration loop driver
- [src/performance_evaluator.py](src/performance_evaluator.py) — accuracy / reliability metrics across iterations
- [src/modules/annotator_agent.py](src/modules/annotator_agent.py) — LLM agent that produces annotations
- [src/modules/sampler_agent.py](src/modules/sampler_agent.py) — selects samples for annotation / review
- [src/modules/auto_reviewer.py](src/modules/auto_reviewer.py) — automated reviewer (proxy or complement to human)
- [src/modules/human_reviewer.py](src/modules/human_reviewer.py) — human-in-the-loop interface
- [src/modules/feedback_parser.py](src/modules/feedback_parser.py) — parses qualitative feedback into structured signals
- [src/modules/prompt_agent.py](src/modules/prompt_agent.py) — refines prompts using parsed feedback
- [src/modules/rag_memory.py](src/modules/rag_memory.py) — RAG memory of past feedback / examples
- [src/modules/annotation_store.py](src/modules/annotation_store.py) — persistence for annotations
- [src/modules/technique_config.py](src/modules/technique_config.py) — prompt technique configuration (few-shot, CoT, structured output, etc.)
- [src/modules/logger.py](src/modules/logger.py) — logging
- [logs/prompts/](logs/prompts/) — versioned prompts across iterations
- [data/](data/), [notebooks/](notebooks/), [docs/](docs/) — datasets, analysis, write-up

Supports multiple LLM backends (e.g. Gemini per recent commits). Current working branch is `rag` — active work on improving the RAG-based feedback memory.

## Working style

- User is doing a research thesis — changes should be reproducible and the effect on metrics (accuracy, iteration convergence, prompt length/complexity) matters. When touching the pipeline, consider whether an experiment run or log change is needed.
- Prefer small, focused edits in existing modules over new abstractions.
